title: GlitchSAT project file (glitchsat.yaml), version 1
description: Describes one chip design, who can do what to it, what must never happen, and how to look for faults. Paths are relative to the folder of the file.

clock.description: The clock input. `none` for a purely combinational design. Omit to auto-detect.

reset.description: The reset input and what happens before the attacker acts. Omit to auto-detect; `none` for no reset.

active.description: Level that resets. Default: low if the name ends in _n/_ni/_b, else high.

cycles.description: How many cycles reset is held at the start. Default 1.

glitch_during_reset.description: false (default): faults start after reset; true: cycle 0 is power-up and faults may hit the reset sequence too.

powerup.description: Flip-flop values at power-up. any: unknown (each may be 0 or 1, the search chooses); zero: all 0; init: the netlist's initial values (error if missing). Default: any when there is a reset, otherwise init where given and 0 elsewhere.

attacker.description: Inputs the attacker controls. Default: every input that is not clock, reset, secret or fixed.

attacker_changes.description: every_cycle (default): a new value each cycle; once: one value for the whole run.

secret.description: Inputs that carry a secret (a key). Held constant; the search may choose any value.

fixed.description: Inputs tied to a value (e.g. scan_en: 0). Strings like "8'hC3" or "0xC3" are accepted.

observe.description: Outputs the attacker can see (default: all outputs). Used by secret-flow checks and reports.

probes.description: Internal signals used in conditions: alias -> hierarchical name (u_ctrl.state_q). They are marked keep before synthesis. Dotted names in conditions become probes automatically.

flows.description: Synthesis flows to analyse. The first is the main one; the others are compared with it (survival across flows). Default: [plain].

analyses.description: What to run. Default: all of them (each one says when it cannot run).

backend.description: auto | py | cadical | kissat | dimacs:/path/to/solver | pysat:NAME

max_state_bits.description: Skip the unbounded proof above this many state bits (default 400).

runs.description: Random simulation runs comparing the analysed netlist with the RTL (default 256).

redact.description: Replace signal and module names by aliases (sig_001, mod_001) in reports.

tasks.description: Named variants (like SymbiYosys tasks): each value overrides keys of this file, e.g. {hardened: {design: {defines: {HARDENED: 1}}}}.

sources.description: Verilog/SystemVerilog files, a gate-level netlist, or {filelist: files.f} (-f style).

top.description: Top module. Omit to auto-detect (the module that nothing instantiates).

frontend.description: auto: .sv -> read_slang (Yosys >= 0.67) else read_verilog -sv; .json -> Yosys JSON netlist.

params.description: Parameter overrides of the top module (like -G).

liberty.description: Liberty files of the standard cells. Read in place, never copied.

stub.description: Verilog with the module's ports only.

blackboxes.description: Modules without a source (encrypted or missing IP). Their outputs become free inputs; the report lists them.

yosys_script.description: Flow `custom`: your Yosys commands after reading the design. Only allow-listed synthesis commands; files read must be inside the project folder. Never: `!`, shell, exec, script, tee, plugin, tcl, python, write_*.

physical_cells.description: Cell-type patterns of physical-only cells (taps, fillers, decaps, diodes) that are dropped before a gate-level netlist is read, and counted. Default for frontend netlist: ['*tap*', '*fill*', '*decap*', '*diode*'].

kind.description: fault (default). secret_flow and masking: format only, not run by this release.

goal.description: What an attacker gets when this check fails; reports take 'what the attacker gets' from it. Default: the template's goal. Without either, reports say the gain was guessed from whole words of the names, or claim none.

bad.description: Verilog expression: true in a cycle where the attack has succeeded.

must_hold.description: Verilog expressions that must be true in every cycle up to the success (e.g. the alarm stays low).

detected_by.description: Shortcut: the attack only counts if this alarm expression stays false (adds !(...) to must_hold).

detect_latency.description: Cycles the alarm may take to react: success must stay unreported this long after it happens.

assertions.description: A checker module file with SVA immediate assert/assume (read with read_verilog -formal); port names = top-level signals.

rule.description: secret_flow: 'src =/=> dst when cond unless cond'.

labels.description: masking: signal -> secret N | static_random | volatile_random | unimportant.

types.description: flip: value inverted for one cycle; set/reset: forced to 1/0 for one cycle. stuck_at_*: accepted as set/reset for one cycle (a permanent fault is not modelled).

where.description: Which outputs can be hit: gate outputs, flip-flop outputs or both (default).

include.description: Only these sites: hierarchy patterns (u_core.*), re:REGEX, or @attribute[=value].

horizon.description: Observation window in cycles (default 20; SymbiYosys uses the same default depth).

per_cycle.description: Not modelled in this release (any number per cycle); must be omitted or null.

cycles.description: Not modelled in this release; must be omitted or null.
